sense: a connection between things or people

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.50: ejus autem vinculum est ratiō et ōrātiō
Cic. Arch. 2: habent quoddam commūne vinclum
terms.comment: Literally a band or a tie; Cicero’s word for what holds things or people together.

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.50: conjungitque nātūrālī quādam societāte

phrases.latin: etenim omnēs artēs quae ad hūmānitātem pertinent habent quoddam commūne vinclum et quasi cognātiōne quādam inter sē continentur
phrases.english: for all the arts that belong to a liberal education have a kind of common link, and are held together, as it were, by family ties

sources: Lewis & Short: vinculum · Lewis & Short: conjunctio · Lewis & Short: conjungo
Cic. Off. 1.50 and Arch. 2 checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
